name: Cyperus

project_scope.admission: Four species reviewed and approved in source pool; not county native certification
project_scope.native_range_status: C. esculentus, C. strigosus, C. odoratus Texas-native at state level, target 3-county status UNRESOLVED. C. rotundus introduced in Texas and NON_NATIVE_COMPARISON; never native metrics.
project_scope.taxonomic_warning: C. odoratus is accepted but FNA's broad odoratus concept includes C. engelmannii; POWO accepts engelmannii separately. Never map engelmannii observations into odoratus without voucher review.

look_here_first: First inspect the crown of the flowering stem: LEAFLIKE BRACTS below several rays bearing crowded SPIKELETS? That supports Cyperus. Then split by underground tubers/stolons versus mature spikelet construction. Yellow vs purple seedhead color ALONE is not a reliable species test.

genus_diagnostics.habit: Sedge herbs, annual or perennial, tufted/rhizomatous/stoloniferous and sometimes bearing tubers. Species may occur along muddy shorelines and ditches or disturbed garden soil.
genus_diagnostics.stem: Culms commonly three-angled but some Cyperus are rounded; the sedge-versus-grass identification cannot rest on 'sedges have edges'.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Leaves commonly basal with closed sheaths and flat, folded, or keeled linear blades. Broad leaflike structures at the top are INVOLUCRAL BRACTS, not ordinary leaves on the upper culm.
genus_diagnostics.inflorescence: Terminal or rarely pseudolateral anthela/umbel-like array with one or more unequal primary RAYS, sometimes secondary rays, bearing clusters of spikelets. Multiple bracts commonly radiate from the base.
genus_diagnostics.flower: Each spikelet bears overlapping scales usually in two rows (distichous), commonly each covering one reduced flower. Check scales under magnification rather than assuming a straw-colored plume is diagnostic.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: One hard one-seeded ACHENE per fertile Cyperus flower; mature achene surfaces, style-branch count and the spikelet rachilla often resolve difficult species.

shared_traits: Cyperaceae family sedge architecture: minute flowers under scales and one-seeded achenes, not grass lemma/palea.
Cyperus typically has basal leaves and an umbrella-like terminal arrangement of rays, bracts and spikelets.
Microscopic spikelet rachilla/scales and subterranean stolons/tubers are frequently species-diagnostic.
priority: 1. Photograph complete inflorescence with bracts, individual rays and spikelets.
2. Photograph one mature spikelet side and face at 1 mm scale; check flattened versus subcylindrical rachilla and whether scales persist.
3. Excavate one complete plant without breaking stolons; check for cormlike base or soft versus hard stolons and tubers.
4. Count style branches and compare mature achenes under magnification.
5. Preserve local provenance and clear nativity separately. Purple nutsedge is an introduced comparison.
study_strategy.warning: Do not key on flowerhead color, triangular stems or habitat alone. C. odoratus FNA-wide concept vs POWO C. engelmannii separation is unresolved in source specimens.

quick_key.if: Tuber-bearing underground stolons; leaves often in rich disturbed soils
quick_key.then: C. esculentus versus C. rotundus — examine stolon texture and mature scale size

quick_key.if: Stolons soft/spongy when dried; tubers commonly 6–11 mm; floral scales usually yellowish-brown 1.8–2.7 mm
quick_key.then: Cyperus esculentus — yellow nutsedge; other traits must support

quick_key.if: Stolons hard/wiry; tubers commonly 3–8 mm; floral scales often purple/reddish-brown 2.6–3.4 mm
quick_key.then: Cyperus rotundus — purple nutsedge, introduced Texas comparison

quick_key.if: Spikelets flattened; basal cormlike swelling; deciduous floral scales commonly 3.2–4.5 mm
quick_key.then: Cyperus strigosus — straw-colored flatsedge; mature material required

quick_key.if: Subcylindrical spikelets; corky winged rachilla disarticulates into 1-fruited segments
quick_key.then: Cyperus odoratus — fragrant/rusty flatsedge; avoid collapsing C. engelmannii concept

quick_key.if: Only a young spikelet or an uprooted stem without underground parts
quick_key.then: Cyperus sp. until mature scale and tuber/rachilla characters available

comparison_matrix.odoratus: No tuber chain required for ID; use mature spikelet
Scale + corky rachilla fragment, not simple individual scale alone
Native state; county UNRESOLVED / concept caution

comparison_cards.title: Yellow nutsedge vs Purple nutsedge
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Carefully lift a single colony with stolons intact and compare the stolon texture; then measure several mature floral scales.
comparison_cards.caution: All ranges and colors overlap; combine multiple traits and preserve non-native status of rotundus.

comparison_cards.title: Straw-colored vs Fragrant flatsedge
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Collect MATURE spikelets. Check whether a scale falls individually from a flattened spikelet or the rachilla breaks into one-fruited corky units.

field_matrix.strigosus: Not fragmented into special one-fruited corky units
field_matrix.odoratus: Corky winged segments disarticulate one achene at a time
Use actual mature rachilla key; basal appearance alone overlaps

comparison_cards.caution: The FNA broad odoratus concept may overlap C. engelmannii under current POWO taxonomy. Recheck voucher before labeling uncertain specimen.

visual_comparison.title: Cyperus: sedge umbrellas, two nutsedges, two flatsedges
visual_comparison.subtitle: NINE physically installed exact-name, source-licensed Cyperus photos were checked as actual JPEGs. These cover flowering heads, several whole/partial plants and underground tubers. No photo currently proves submillimeter scale size or the special C. odoratus corky one-fruited rachilla.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: BRACTS + RAYS + SPIKELETS = FLATSEDGE PATTERN. TUBER/STOLON (esculentus/rotundus) vs MATURE SPIKELET RACHILLA (strigosus/odoratus) names the species.

part_examples.title: 1 · See the umbrella of bracts and rays
part_examples.look_for: Long leaflike INVOLUCRAL BRACTS spread from just beneath the cluster. Above them, unequal stalks (RAYS) carry smaller bunches of spikelets. Don't confuse a bract with a basal leaf.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Find the typical flatsedge silhouette before trying to name a species.

part_examples.title: 2 · Spot packed spikelets on a flatsedge head
part_examples.look_for: Look at several round, starburst-like heads and the numerous packed narrow SPIKELETS radiating from them. Individual two-ranked scales are too small to confirm from this general view—request a detached same-mm close-up.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Cyperus spikelet architecture is far more reliable than the plant looking vaguely grass-like.

part_examples.title: 3 · Compare yellow nutsedge aboveground
part_examples.look_for: The yellow-brown heads of C. esculentus look distinct at first, but color fades with age. Follow the stolon underground for stronger evidence.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The right species decision requires tubers + stolon texture + measured scales, not just color.

part_examples.title: 4 · See harvested yellow nutsedge tubers
part_examples.look_for: This verified image is a PILE of harvested, dried yellow nutsedge tubers. It teaches the look of the storage organ, but the actual underground soft stolon connection is not visible. A fully excavated same-plant photo is still needed.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Separates the underground growth strategy from ordinary fibrous roots.

part_examples.title: 5 · Compare purple nutsedge flowering head
part_examples.look_for: C. rotundus commonly has red-brown to purplish persistent floral scales, but hue overlaps yellow nutsedge and is a supporting character only.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Tuber/stolon combinations are more reliable than calling every reddish sedge purple nutsedge.

part_examples.title: 6 · Compare purple nutsedge's tuber
part_examples.role: purple nutsedge tuber / hard stolon needed
part_examples.look_for: The verified photo shows a purple nutsedge tuber connected by a thin dark horizontal underground runner to a shoot. Locate the tuber and stolon; the expected HARD/WIRY texture still needs a specimen in hand.
part_examples.why_it_matters: The underground character is a key field split from yellow nutsedge.

part_examples.title: 7 · Find reddish spikelet clusters
part_examples.look_for: Verified photo of several reddish clusters bearing many narrow spikelets, NOT a detached single-scale macro. A true 1 mm side-view of one mature spikelet is still a photo target.
part_examples.why_it_matters: A close-up can teach scales, rachilla and flower units that whole-head portraits hide.

part_examples.title: 8 · Locate fragrant flatsedge's rays and bracts
part_examples.role: fragrant flatsedge rays / mature rachilla needs macro
part_examples.look_for: The photo shows the upper flowering head with radiating green bracts and narrow spikelet clusters. It does not show the underground base or the decisive corky segmented rachilla.
part_examples.why_it_matters: Sets up the FNA C. odoratus separation without pretending a broad habit photo proves microscopic segments.

part_examples.title: 9 · NEED PHOTO — jointed rachilla vs deciduous scales
part_examples.look_for: Matched mature C. odoratus segments showing corky wings and one achene versus C. strigosus flattened spikelets with deciduous scales and a cormlike plant base. Include 1 mm ruler.
part_examples.why_it_matters: This is the highest-value fine botanical separator for the flatsedge pair.

visual_comparison.annotation_policy: Photo subjects individually inspected against role labels. NO arrows are installed or approved. Single-scales, achenes, stigma branches, actual rachilla segments and matched underground stolon texture need future macroscopic/microscopic captures.
